chapters.title: Financial models become executable algorithms
chapters.purpose: Translate bonds, options, and portfolio decisions into inputs, outputs, invariants, and a reproducible Python/R workflow.

chapters.title: Rates, approximations, and numerical reliability
chapters.purpose: Discount cash flows consistently; interpolate curves; derive Taylor remainders; separate problem conditioning from algorithmic error. Pilot chapter.

chapters.title: Portfolio choice and the first numerical workshop
chapters.purpose: Solve safe/risky allocation by analytic and grid methods, then check the first bond, interpolation, and logarithm workshops.

chapters.title: Linear systems and identifiable portfolio weights
chapters.purpose: Develop matrix algebra, elimination, factorization, residuals, and ill-conditioned target-return constraints.

chapters.title: Covariance and the geometry of risk
chapters.purpose: Build covariance from returns; prove positive semidefiniteness; interpret eigenvalues, diversification, and nearly null directions.

chapters.title: Market factors, regression, and implementation
chapters.purpose: Explain CAPM assumptions, factor models, estimation, and paired R/Python matrix labs.

chapters.title: Option payoffs and functions
chapters.purpose: Distinguish payoff from profit and value; define European/American claims; use piecewise functions and software functions.

chapters.title: Replication and binomial valuation
chapters.purpose: Derive one-period replication and risk-neutral weights; extend by backward induction; solve worked examples.

chapters.title: Path dependence and option laboratories
chapters.purpose: Explain exotic payoffs and implement valuation functions; distinguish path/state from terminal-price-only claims.

chapters.title: Financial equations as inverse problems
chapters.purpose: Separate price, yield, and implied volatility; derive bracketing and existence/identifiability; interpret volatility surfaces.

chapters.title: Newton, secant, and safeguarded calibration
chapters.purpose: Derive local convergence and failure modes; choose stopping rules with price/parameter meaning; solve worked problems.

chapters.title: Constructing curves and volatility surfaces
chapters.purpose: Bootstrap and interpolate under consistent conventions; test basic static arbitrage and make R/Python implementations inspectable.

chapters.title: Bond calculus, duration, and convexity
chapters.purpose: Differentiate prices under a specified yield convention; distinguish clean/dirty price; check finite-difference Greeks.

chapters.title: Portfolio objectives and expected utility
chapters.purpose: Derive first/second-order conditions and utility comparisons; make certainty equivalents and risk aversion explicit.

chapters.title: Numerical integration for financial expectations
chapters.purpose: Derive trapezoidal and Simpson quadrature; analyze discretization errors and implement convergence diagnostics in R/Python.

chapters.title: Geometric Brownian motion and Black–Scholes
chapters.purpose: Derive lognormal transitions and model price; distinguish real-world and pricing measures; check limiting cases.

chapters.title: Finite differences and early exercise
chapters.purpose: Derive the Black–Scholes grid, boundary conditions, stability restrictions, and American obstacle problem.

chapters.title: A reproducible option-pricing laboratory
chapters.purpose: Reconcile binomial, GBM, and PDE implementations; test convergence rather than compare unexplained output.

chapters.title: Equality-constrained mean–variance portfolios
chapters.purpose: Solve the Markowitz block system and derive the efficient frontier/capital-market line under stated assumptions.

chapters.title: Inequality constraints and optimality certificates
chapters.purpose: Derive KKT conditions, active sets, and their limitations; apply the optimization tutorials.

chapters.title: Arbitrage detection by linear programming
chapters.purpose: Formulate finite-market arbitrage consistently; connect primal portfolios and dual state prices; run R/Python checks.

chapters.title: Random walks, sampling, and Monte Carlo
chapters.purpose: Build random variables from a generator; derive Brownian scaling and Monte Carlo estimator variance; distinguish sampling and path error.

chapters.title: Monte Carlo option prices and uncertain parameters
chapters.purpose: Compute European payoffs with confidence intervals; use variance reduction; separate parameter uncertainty and simulation noise.

chapters.title: Asian options and a complete numerical workflow
chapters.purpose: Integrate course synthesis, path-dependent Monte Carlo, R/Python/Colab labs, validation, and uncertainty reporting.
